paraphrases.title: Wall-mount ESP32 box with LED light pipes
paraphrases.request: Wall-mount box for an ESP32 DevKitC V4 board, 54.4 x 27.9 mm, no mounting holes. Micro-USB at one short end, PCB antenna at the other. Two mounting ears for 4.2 mm countersunk wood screws, slots 100 mm apart; each slot keeps at least 3 mm from the ear edge and from the box. Three 5 mm LEDs in the lid, flush with the outside, retained. Micro-USB cable plugs in through one short end, lid on. Antenna end stays clear: nothing over the antenna, at least 8 mm free past the board end. Lid fixed with M3 self-tapping screws. FDM, PLA, printed back face down.
paraphrases.request_verbatim: A wall-mounted ESP32 enclosure with two mounting ears taking 4.2 mm countersunk wood screws, 100 mm apart. Three 5 mm LEDs shine through the lid; the LEDs sit flush with the outside and must not fall out. The ear slots must leave at least 3 mm to the box edge.
paraphrases.request_notes: Added to the brief (derived, see requirements.md 3.1 and 3.2): the board has no holes so it rests on four pads and is located by walls and stops (FD2); 'LED light pipes' = each LED in a collar in the lid, dome flush, flange captured and a snap lip behind it (FD5); 'to the box edge' = to the ear's free edges and to the box wall (FD4); '100 mm apart' = between slot centres (FD3); lid closure = four M3 screws in tabs outside the cavity (FD1); antenna numbers (8 mm beyond, 5 mm above the module) from the ESP32 catalogue part; FDM, PLA (A7).

l1.text: Place the catalogue ESP32 DevKitC V4 with its micro-USB port at the −X short end and the antenna pointing +X, put three 5 mm LEDs on the lid, keep all parts from colliding, and declare the layout.

Four pads under the end regions of the board carry it, outside the header footprint, each 10 mm² or more. Walls and two stops at the antenna end locate it; stops sit 0.2 to 1.0 mm off the board and lower than its top face. The printed box stays out of the board's keep-out volumes: header pins, tails, component side.

Keep walls and lid out of the antenna keep-out zone, and make the cavity reach at least 8.0 mm past the antenna end of the board. The zone, taken from the part data, is the last 6.0 mm of the board plus the 8.0 mm beyond it, across the whole board width, rising 5.0 mm above the module top.

Lid closed, a micro-USB cable must seat fully in the board via a single opening in the −X end wall, with 0.3 mm or more spare around the plug. Wall around the opening: 1.5 mm minimum. The opening may exceed the plug by at most 1.5 mm per side.

Three 5 mm LEDs sit in collars in the lid, domes flush with the outer face, flanges trapped between a shoulder and a snap lip so they cannot come out. Holes 5.2 to 5.4 mm wide; flange overlap 0.2 mm or more per side; domes within 0.3 mm of flush; snap-lip opening 5.3 to 5.6 mm with two or more slits. LEDs in a row, 10.0 mm or more apart, each axis 4.5 mm or more in plan from the header-pin and antenna keep-outs of the board.

Two ears on the box, each with a countersunk slot for a 4.2 mm wood screw. Slot centres 100.0 mm apart. From every countersink outline, at least 3.0 mm to the ear edge and to the box. Slot shape: stadium, 4.5 mm wide, 4.0 mm between end centres for adjustment, under a 90 degree countersink 8.4 mm across. Ears 3.5 to 5.0 mm thick. Slot centres symmetric about the box centre to within 0.5 mm.
Flat back face on the box; the ears lie in the same plane, flat to 0.3 mm, so it sits flush on the wall.

Lid is its own body, located on the base by a sliding lip and fastened with four M3 self-tapping screws into tabs outside the cavity. Screw axes 3.5 to 5.0 mm past the outer face of the wall; pilots 2.4 to 2.6 mm, 6.0 mm deep or more; lid holes 3.4 mm. Sliding lip 2.0 mm deep or more, 0.15 to 0.35 mm clearance each side.

With the lid on, the only openings are the USB opening, three LED holes, the lid screw holes and two ear slots. Walls, floor and lid 2.0 to 4.0 mm thick. 1.5 mm or more of material around each opening.
Base prints back face down, lid prints outer face down; each is a single manifold body, no supports.
Closed box including ears and tabs: 125 x 50 x 26 mm maximum, longest dimension along the board's 54.4 mm side.
Deliver a base STL, a lid STL, the OpenSCAD source, the declared layout and the agent's clearance report; the report must match an independent measurement.

paraphrases.title: Wall-mount ESP32 box with LED light pipes
paraphrases.request: I'm after a housing that goes on a wall and holds an ESP32 DevKitC V4 dev board (it measures 54.4 x 27.9 mm and has no screw holes; the micro-USB connector is on one short end and the PCB antenna on the opposite one). The housing gets two mounting ears for 4.2 mm countersunk wood screws, with the two screw slots 100 mm from each other, and each slot has to stay at least 3 mm clear of the ear's edge and of the box itself. Up top, three 5 mm LEDs shine out through the lid, sitting flush with its outer surface and unable to fall out. I want to plug a micro-USB cable into one short end while the lid is on. Don't cover the antenna end: no wall or lid above the antenna, and at least 8 mm of open space past the end of the board. The lid is fastened with M3 self-tapping screws. I'll print it in PLA on an FDM printer with the back face on the bed.
paraphrases.request_verbatim: A wall-mounted ESP32 enclosure with two mounting ears taking 4.2 mm countersunk wood screws, 100 mm apart. Three 5 mm LEDs shine through the lid; the LEDs sit flush with the outside and must not fall out. The ear slots must leave at least 3 mm to the box edge.
paraphrases.request_notes: Added to the brief (derived, see requirements.md 3.1 and 3.2): the board has no holes so it rests on four pads and is located by walls and stops (FD2); 'LED light pipes' = each LED in a collar in the lid, dome flush, flange captured and a snap lip behind it (FD5); 'to the box edge' = to the ear's free edges and to the box wall (FD4); '100 mm apart' = between slot centres (FD3); lid closure = four M3 screws in tabs outside the cavity (FD1); antenna numbers (8 mm beyond, 5 mm above the module) from the ESP32 catalogue part; FDM, PLA (A7).

l1.text: Using the catalogue, the design positions the ESP32 DevKitC V4 so the micro-USB port faces the short end at −X and the antenna points toward +X; it also puts three 5 mm LEDs in the lid. Nothing may collide, and the layout has to be declared.

Support the board on four pads beneath its two end regions, away from the header footprint, every pad no smaller than 10 mm². The walls plus two stops at the antenna end hold it in place, the stops being 0.2 to 1.0 mm away from the board and under its top face. None of the printed box may intrude on the board's keep-out volumes (header pins, tails, component side).

The antenna keep-out must stay empty of walls and lid. Per the part's data it covers the final 6.0 mm of the board and the 8.0 mm past its end, spanning the board's full width and reaching up to 5.0 mm over the top of the module; the cavity must run at least 8.0 mm beyond the antenna end.

It must be possible to push a micro-USB cable all the way into the board, lid on, through one hole in the end wall at −X. The hole gives the plug at least 0.3 mm of room all the way round, but is no more than 1.5 mm larger than the plug on any side, and at least 1.5 mm of wall remains around it.

In the lid, each of three 5 mm LEDs goes into a collar so its dome is level with the outer surface and its flange is caught by a shoulder with a snap lip behind, which keeps the LED from dropping out. The collar holes measure 5.2 to 5.4 mm across, the flange overlaps by at least 0.2 mm each side, the dome is within 0.3 mm of flush, and the snap-lip opening is 5.3 to 5.6 mm with at least two slits. Arrange the LEDs in a line with at least 10.0 mm between them, and keep every LED axis at least 4.5 mm (in plan) from the board's header-pin and antenna keep-outs.

The box gets a pair of ears, and each carries a countersunk slot sized for a 4.2 mm wood screw. The centres of the two slots are 100.0 mm from each other, and the countersink outline of each slot stays at least 3.0 mm away from its ear's edge and from the box. Every slot is a stadium 4.5 mm wide with 4.0 mm between the centres of its ends (so you can adjust), beneath a 90 degree countersink that is 8.4 mm across. Make the ears 3.5 to 5.0 mm thick, with the slot centres symmetric about the centre of the box to within 0.5 mm.
So the box can lie flat on the wall, its back should be a flat face and the ears must be coplanar with it, within 0.3 mm.

Make the lid a separate piece that sits on the base via a sliding lip and is secured by four M3 self-tapping screws that go into tabs outside the cavity. The screw axes lie 3.5 to 5.0 mm outside the wall's outer face, the pilot holes are 2.4 to 2.6 mm across and at least 6.0 mm deep, and the lid's holes are 3.4 mm. The lip should be at least 2.0 mm deep, with 0.15 to 0.35 mm of clearance on each side.

Once closed, the box may be open only at the USB port, the three LED holes, the screw holes for the lid and the two slots in the ears. Wall, floor and lid thickness should fall between 2.0 and 4.0 mm, and every opening needs at least 1.5 mm of surrounding material.
Each part must be one manifold body that prints without supports: the base resting on its back face and the lid on its outer face.
Overall, counting ears and tabs, the shut box must fit within 125 x 50 x 26 mm, with the long direction running along the 54.4 mm side of the board.
What comes back is a base STL and a lid STL, the OpenSCAD source, the layout declaration, and the agent's own clearance report, whose figures have to agree with an independent measurement.
